sources_considered.why: Goldman Sachs Research's tally of hyperscaler and AI-related debt issuance.
Single-company evidence of GPUs staged without power.
A secondary summary of the same debt figures. Goldman's own page was preferred.

evidence_items.locator: transcript, Amanda Lynam's answer on why hyperscalers use bond markets

receipt.public_excerpt: These companies, the group of hyperscalers, issued $108 billion of debt globally in 2025. Fast-forward to 2026. So far this year, they've issued $194 billion.

evidence_items.explanation: Hyperscalers alone issued about $302 billion of debt from 2025 to early August 2026. That supports the 'hundreds of billions of dollars of debt' part.

evidence_items.locator: transcript, Amanda Lynam on the broader AI ecosystem

receipt.public_excerpt: By our estimates, we track nearly $500 billion of AI-related debt issuance

evidence_items.explanation: Broader AI-related debt issuance of nearly $500 billion in 2026 to date also supports the debt part.

evidence_items.locator: Note on segment information, customer concentration paragraph

receipt.public_excerpt: Our revenue is concentrated among a limited number of direct and indirect customers

evidence_items.explanation: NVIDIA confirms its revenue is concentrated in a few customers. That fits the 'handful of companies' part. It says nothing about whether those customers use the GPUs.

evidence_items.publisher: Crypto Briefing (citing ZeroHedge and Business Insider)
evidence_items.locator: section 'Racks arriving faster than the grid can keep up', paragraph 3

receipt.public_excerpt: Some of these racks are being staged in facilities with plenty of floor space but not enough power supply to activate them.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that one big buyer had some racks idle for lack of power. That is far short of showing the large buyers are 'for the most part' not using their GPUs.

unresolved_gaps: No representative evidence shows whether most GPUs bought by the largest buyers were unused at the time of the post. This is the central charge.
Consumer electronics price data and stock-market dependence were not measured. Those parts are largely rhetorical.
Debt totals are bank estimates whose definitions vary.
